runtime.execution: Tokio TUI/orchestrator plus per-agent bounded mpsc task and broadcast output; native file/shell calls use blocking std APIs inside async methods.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns local sessions/tool permissions and child MCP processes; consumes Ollama and MCP endpoints.

summary: Early Rust multi-agent manager with three native tools, shared operator focus and persisted chat; several claimed control paths are incomplete.

inspection.scope: Entry→per-agent mailbox→Ollama streaming→approval/tool dispatch→message state and continuation; session/model switch, event routing, MCP connection registry and tests.
inspection.limits: Source read only, reference not executed. No runtime execution. Model-switch announcement does not update captured agent_model; automatically preapproved tool execution does not schedule its own continuation. Model-to-model messaging/cancellation/refit not established in exposed registry.

evidence.claim: Tokio entry uses Ollama and truncates diagnostic log at startup.
write_file/read_file/run_shell_command; shell waits for output without PTY or handle, successful stderr omitted.
Creates per-agent task/mailbox, restores session/model, forwards output separately.
Mailbox serially awaits model chat/approval; continue event invokes another chat.
Preapproved tools execute serially; outputs added as user text; no automatic continuation event on this branch.
Approval can be once/session/global; allowed branch enqueues ContinueConversation; denial writes user text.
SwitchModel changes orchestrator field and announces success but not captured worker agent_model.
Serializes session state via pid temporary file then rename; this is chat/settings persistence.
Events carry source/destination/SystemTime and ephemeral bounded broadcast bus.
MCP command discovery registers tool adapters using named connection IDs.
MCP tool adapter forwards registered names/args to shared connection registry.
Only Ollama factory implemented; future provider comment is not provider support.
Permission save/reload in two separate temporary directories; does not attack concurrent shared-file writes.
Operator input/approval routes to active agent and agent switch selects/creates tasks.
Program API can address a worker ID via send_event_to_agent; not itself a model tool.

tests.focus: Registry schema/profile and mocked file/shell calls
tests.oracle: Tool names/profiles/results compared to mocks; tests do not establish real process cancellation or filesystem boundaries.
Save/reload exact allowset under independent TempDirs, not shared concurrent writers.
Program prints live provider response; no assertion of agent loop correctness and not executed here.

strengths: Per-worker mailbox and output forwarding make lifecycle ownership visible.
Session/global standing named authority can eliminate repeated prompts.
limits: No runtime execution. Model-switch announcement does not update captured agent_model; automatically preapproved tool execution does not schedule its own continuation. Model-to-model messaging/cancellation/refit not established in exposed registry.
arconaut_questions: What oracle catches the preapproved-tool continuation branch diverging from approved-once execution?
How should addressed model messages and cancellation bypass a worker awaiting its provider request?
